info.name: Incident Response Service (UC4)
info.description:
Drives the incident-response process end to end and covers every decision path,
every boundary event and both escalation timers.

Folder 1 raises an incident, one request per classification scenario; each saves {{incidentId}}.
Folder 3 lists and completes human tasks using one shared body (extra variables are ignored, so
the same body works for any task). Folder 4 has the exact form fields per task if you'd rather
demo it properly. Folder 5 is the error responses. Folder 6 is the failure and timer paths: AI
connector failure, isolation failure, the CISO SLA timer and the 72h regulatory timer, plus the
ad-hoc action variants.

Happy path: raise a P1, wait ~25-30s for the automated chain to reach the human tasks, list active
tasks (saves {{taskKey}} and {{taskKey2}}), then complete. The parallel phase has two tasks open at
once so use both keys; everything after it has one, so 'Complete active task' is enough. Re-list
between phases until it comes back empty, then check the incident is CLOSED.

Phase order: [Containment + Forensic] -> CISO Review -> Integrity Verification -> File Regulatory
Notification -> Incident Closure.

Responses are wrapped in {"data":..., "meta":...}; errors are RFC 7807 problem details.
{{baseUrl}} defaults to http://localhost:8080.

request.description: UP also means the connection to the cluster is healthy.
Swagger UI is at {{baseUrl}}/swagger-ui/index.html

item.name: 1 - Raise incident (classification scenarios)
item.description: title and source are required; attackConfirmed, assetCriticality (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL), dataExposed and recordCount are optional and steer the two DMNs. Leave them out and you get confirmed / HIGH / exposed / 25000, i.e. a P1 that needs regulatory notification.

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| expect severity P1, regulatory notification REQUIRED');

request.description: No signals, so the service defaults kick in (confirmed / HIGH / exposed / 25000) and the DMN says P1. Regulatory notification is required. Full response path with every human task.

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| expect severity P1 (CRITICAL asset)');

request.description: CRITICAL matches earlier in the table than the HIGH+exposed rule, so this is P1 regardless of whether data was exposed. 120000 records means Legal has to file.

item.name: P2 - HIGH asset, no data exposed

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| expect severity P2; File Regulatory Notification SKIPPED (dataExposed=false)');

request.description: The interesting one: still P1, but the regulatory table needs recordCount >= 500 and 120 falls through to the default false. Shows the two DMNs are independent decisions.

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| expect severity P4 -> AUTO_CLOSED, no human tasks. Wait ~15s then run Get incident.');

request.description: attackConfirmed=false hits the first rule (hit policy is FIRST), so P4, and the gateway routes straight to Auto Close. No branches, no human tasks. Give it ~15s then check Get incident says AUTO_CLOSED.

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| expect first task = Handle Isolation Failure (incident-commander)');

request.description: The isolate worker throws a BPMN error, the boundary event inside Containment catches it, and Handle Isolation Failure lands with the commander instead of Containment Verification. This is boundary event 1 of 5; the other four are in folder 6.

item.name: 4 - Per-task bodies (exact form fields)
item.description: One request per task with only that task's fields, taken from src/main/resources/forms. They all point at {{taskKey}}, so list the tasks first and fire the one matching the name that gets logged.

request.description: Only shows up if you raised with forceIsolationFailure.
Containment branch of the parallel gateway.
Forensics branch. Point it at {{taskKey2}} if this one came back second in the list.
After the join. The SLA boundary timer escalates if this sits too long, without cancelling the task.
Inside Recovery, after Restore Services.
Only appears when the regulatory DMN returns true, i.e. data exposed and at least 500 records. Has the 72h timer on it.

exec: console.log(pm.response.json().data, '-> now run Get incident, expect CLOSED');

item.name: 5 - Negative tests (validation & business errors)
item.description:
RFC 7807 problem details: bean validation gives 400 with fieldErrors, BusinessException gives 422 with an errorCode, and a body or path parameter the framework can't even parse gives 400 with rejectedValue.

The first block is the required fields and unknown ids. The second is the optional fields - assetCriticality, recordCount and the three demo overrides from folder 6 are all validated at the boundary, because an unparseable duration or an element id that isn't in the ad-hoc sub-process would otherwise fail the process instance minutes later instead of failing the request.

request.description: title is @NotBlank, so this comes back as a problem detail with a fieldErrors entry.

item.name: Raise with blank title and source -> 400 (two field errors)

request.description: Whitespace-only and empty both fail @NotBlank, so you get two entries.
Well-formed UUID that doesn't exist. BusinessException maps to 422 with a stable errorCode.

item.name: List tasks for unknown incident -> 422 INCIDENT_NOT_FOUND

request.description: The task endpoints resolve the incident first, so they fail the same way.

item.name: Complete active task with none / two active -> 422

request.description: Run it right after a P4 raise for NO_ACTIVE_TASK, or during a P1's parallel phase for AMBIGUOUS_TASK.

Needs any existing {{incidentId}}. The engine returns 404 for a key that doesn't exist or was already completed; the adapter translates it, so it comes back as a business error rather than a 500. Completing the same task twice hits this too.

Jackson can't parse it, so bean validation never runs. The framework handler has no case for this and would return 500; IncidentWebExceptionHandler claims it and returns 400 with the parse error in rejectedValue.
recordCount is an Integer. Deserialisation fails before validation, so this is the same handler as malformed JSON, not a fieldErrors response.

item.name: Path id that isn't a UUID -> 400

request.description: Different from 'unknown incident': that one is a well-formed UUID that doesn't exist (422), this one never converts to a UUID at all (400). Worth showing both.

The DMN only has rules for LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL. Without this check 'EXTREME' would silently fall through to the catch-all rule and come back P3, which looks like the table is wrong rather than the request.
A negative count of exposed records is meaningless, and the regulatory DMN compares it against 500.

The timer boundary needs an ISO-8601 duration. '20 seconds' would be accepted at the API and then fail when Zeebe evaluates =slaDuration to create the timer, i.e. an incident in Operate on a token nobody is watching. Rejecting it here turns a stuck process into a typo.
'P' is the ISO-8601 prefix with no units, which the pattern rejects. Same reasoning as slaDuration.

exec: console.log('field:', fe[0] && fe[0].field, '| rejected:', fe[0] && fe[0].rejectedValue);

request.description: Only Task_BlockIp, Task_RevokeCredentials and Task_DeployPatch exist inside the ad-hoc sub-process. The error names the index, e.g. responseActions[1], so you can tell which entry is wrong. An unknown id would otherwise fail the ad-hoc activation at runtime.

item.name: 6 - Boundary events, timers & ad-hoc actions
item.description:
One request per boundary event in the model, plus the ad-hoc variants.

The model has five boundary events:
  1. Isolation Failed (error)      on Isolate Systems            -> forceIsolationFailure
  2. AI failed (error)             on AI Threat Triage           -> forceAiFailure
  3. AI failed (error)             on AI Post-Incident Report    -> forceAiFailure
  4. SLA breach (timer, non-int.)  on CISO Review                -> slaDuration
  5. 72h deadline (timer, non-int.) on File Regulatory Notification -> regulatoryDeadline

forceAiFailure points the AI Agent tasks at a model id OpenAI rejects, so the connector really
fails, errorExpression really raises AI_STEP_FAILED, and the fallback worker really runs.
slaDuration and regulatoryDeadline replace the PT4H / PT72H timers with something you can wait
for. Both timers are NON-INTERRUPTING: the user task stays open and the main flow carries on, so
after the escalation you still complete the task normally.

Every one of these leaves a row in GET /incidents/{id}/tasks/outcomes with completedBy
'system:process' - that is the assertion surface. Run 'Verify boundary & timer events' after each.

item.name: AI triage failure -> fallback worker (fast, P4)

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| AI triage boundary should fire, then P4 -> AUTO_CLOSED. Wait ~20s, then run Verify boundary & timer events.');

body.raw:
{
  "title": "AI triage failure demo",
  "source": "SIEM",
  "forceAiFailure": true,
  "attackConfirmed": false,
  "assetCriticality": "LOW",
  "dataExposed": false,
  "recordCount": 0
}

request.description: Isolates boundary event 2 on its own. The AI call fails, Boundary_TriageAiFailed routes to the triage worker anyway, and attackConfirmed=false makes it a P4 so it auto-closes in seconds without any human tasks. Expect an 'AI threat triage fallback' outcome row and status AUTO_CLOSED.

item.name: AI failure on both steps -> drive to CLOSED (P2)

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| both AI boundaries fire. Drive it with folder 3: 2 parallel tasks -> CISO Review -> Integrity Verification -> Incident Closure (P2 skips Legal).');

body.raw:
{
  "title": "AI unavailable end to end",
  "source": "EDR",
  "forceAiFailure": true,
  "attackConfirmed": true,
  "assetCriticality": "HIGH",
  "dataExposed": false,
  "recordCount": 0
}

request.description: Boundary events 2 and 3 in one run. P2 so the regulatory branch is skipped and you reach the post-incident report step in four completions. At the end the outcomes list has both 'AI threat triage fallback' and 'AI post-incident report fallback', and the incident still reaches CLOSED - the point being that an LLM outage degrades the process instead of stopping it.

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| complete the 2 parallel tasks, then LEAVE CISO Review open for ~25s. Then run Verify boundary & timer events.');

body.raw:
{
  "title": "SLA breach demo - unattended P1",
  "source": "SIEM",
  "slaDuration": "PT20S",
  "attackConfirmed": true,
  "assetCriticality": "CRITICAL",
  "dataExposed": false,
  "recordCount": 0
}

request.description: Boundary event 4. Normally a P1 gives the CISO PT4H; slaDuration overrides that to 20 seconds. The timer starts when CISO Review is created, i.e. after the parallel join, so complete Containment Verification and Forensic Analysis first, then wait. Non-interrupting, so CISO Review is still there afterwards and you can complete it as usual. Expect a 'SLA breach escalation (CISO review)' outcome row.

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| drive to File Regulatory Notification, then leave it open ~25s.');

request.description: Boundary event 5, the one with the actual regulatory teeth. 25000 records exposed means the regulatory DMN returns true and Legal gets File Regulatory Notification. Complete everything up to it (parallel pair -> CISO Review -> Integrity Verification), then sit on it for 20s. Non-interrupting, so Legal keeps the task; the escalation just tells the CISO the clock ran out. Expect a 'Regulatory deadline escalation (72h)' outcome row.

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| all three ad-hoc tasks activate. Check Operate: Block IP, Revoke Credentials, Deploy Patch all completed inside the ad-hoc sub-process.');

request.description: The default only activates Block IP and Revoke Credentials, so Deploy Patch is never exercised. This picks all three. Valid element ids are Task_BlockIp, Task_RevokeCredentials, Task_DeployPatch - the ad-hoc sub-process activates exactly what you list, which is the modelling point: the commander chooses the actions, the process doesn't dictate them.

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| only Block IP runs in the ad-hoc sub-process.');

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Minimal response - block the C2 address only",
  "source": "Threat Intel",
  "responseActions": ["Task_BlockIp"],
  "attackConfirmed": true,
  "assetCriticality": "MEDIUM",
  "dataExposed": false,
  "recordCount": 0
}

request.description: The other end of the ad-hoc range: one action. Proves the branch completes on whatever subset was activated rather than waiting for a fixed set.

item.name: Every boundary event in one run (full sweep)

exec: console.log('incidentId =', d.id, '| expect, in order: AI triage fallback -> Handle Isolation Failure task -> SLA escalation at CISO Review -> 72h escalation at Legal -> AI report fallback -> CLOSED.');

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Worst-case incident - everything that can go wrong does",
  "source": "SIEM",
  "forceIsolationFailure": true,
  "forceAiFailure": true,
  "slaDuration": "PT20S",
  "regulatoryDeadline": "PT20S",
  "responseActions": ["Task_BlockIp", "Task_RevokeCredentials", "Task_DeployPatch"],
  "attackConfirmed": true,
  "assetCriticality": "CRITICAL",
  "dataExposed": true,
  "recordCount": 25000
}

request.description:
All five boundary events plus every ad-hoc action, on one incident.

Walkthrough: AI triage fails -> fallback. Containment isolation fails -> Handle Isolation Failure (commander) instead of going straight to Containment Verification, so the parallel phase opens Handle Isolation Failure + Forensic Analysis, then Containment Verification. After the join, park on CISO Review for 25s to trip the SLA timer, complete it, then Integrity Verification, then park on File Regulatory Notification for 25s to trip the deadline timer. Complete it, AI report fails -> fallback, Incident Closure -> CLOSED.

Verify boundary & timer events should then list four system rows.

exec: console.log('Boundary / timer events:', system.map(o => o.taskName + ' @ ' + o.elementId).join(' | ') || '(none yet)');
pm.test('at least one boundary or timer event recorded', () => pm.expect(system.length).to.be.above(0));

request.description:
Same endpoint as folder 3, read the other way round. Rows with completedBy 'system:process' and userTaskKey 0 are the automated ones: AI fallbacks and timer escalations. Everything else is a human completion. The isolation-failure boundary is the exception - it produces a real user task (Handle Isolation Failure), so it shows up as a human row.

Allow ~20s after raising before expecting a fallback row, and slaDuration/regulatoryDeadline plus a few seconds for the timers.
